classification.note: Read-only analysis. No header and no source published: every finding is a defect localisation in existing host bindings plus a correction to two merged documents, and the only new pure rule (swim speed = WaterTravelSpeed * 0.6) is one multiply that src/game_hosts_gunnery.cpp already performs inline for the range. The project built and its single existing test passed, but nothing in this packet changed compiled code. NO RUN-TIME EVIDENCE: bsp_game.exe aborts with 0xC0000005 immediately after 'Phase 5 load_game_settings' on this machine this turn, for both this worktree's build and the main checkout's prebuilt binary, so docs/WORKER_VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST.md rule 6 is unsatisfied and every claim is static.

question: 16 torpedoes launch on the 3200-frame USN02 mission and none hits; arc_blocked is 40017 on 71 mounts. What does 008FBB00 solve, with which speed, is the host passing the right one, is 40017 faithful, and is 0 of 16 faithful?

verdict.what_008fbb00_solves: a plain constant-velocity lead. 008FB8D0 solves the intercept quadratic for a projectile flying straight at a constant speed against a target extrapolated linearly from one velocity sample; 008FBB00 returns target + t * target_velocity. No turn rate, no acceleration, no gravity, no iteration. On failure it returns AL=0 and does not write the out vector; 00900263 checks it.
verdict.speed_it_uses: descriptor+0E4h = WaterTravelSpeed (51.444 m/s for the Mark 15), loaded at 0090022B. NOT the muzzle V0 at descriptor+50h (13), which is what the AAFlakBot's solver call at 009031CF takes from the same node.
verdict.host_passes: wrong. src/game_hosts_gunnery.cpp:1191 passes gun.muzzle_speed, which src/game_hosts_gunnery.cpp:436 fills from the flattened 'v0' key, which src/game_hosts_gunnery.cpp:296 fills from bc.V0 - the bullet class V0, i.e. descriptor+50h.
verdict.consequence_of_the_wrong_speed: with s = 13 the quadratic coefficient a = |v|^2 - s^2 is positive and disc = b*b - 4ac >= 0 requires cos^2(theta) >= 4 - 4 s^2/u^2, which has no solution for any target faster than 2s/sqrt(3) = 15.01 m/s. A Fletcher at 18.777 m/s is past it, so 008FB8D0 answers 0 for every aspect, the host falls back to lead = at (src/game_hosts_gunnery.cpp:1194) and aims at the target's present position.
verdict.arc_blocked_40017: not faithful, and not 40017 refused shots. It is a per-tick counter (src/game_hosts_gunnery.cpp:1294-1300) with a ceiling of 71*3200 = 227200. Every torpedo platform in vehicleclasses.lua authors exactly one window with MinVertAngle == MaxVertAngle == 0 and a 50-68 degree horizontal broadside sector, so a narrow window is real; but the refusals are dominated by two host modelling errors: the host commands a non-zero vertical where 009003DD passes 0.0f, and it lets gun_set_target_angles_0085aba0 refuse where the native first snaps the heading up to pi/4 onto the nearest firing-window edge through 0085AB50 -> 007F6190.
verdict.expected_hit_rate: against a 110 m 18.777 m/s destroyer: about 7% of aspects at 637 m, 3% at 1000 m and 1.3% at 1852 m with the native solver and the native speed; 0% with the host's current s = 13. A few per cent, concentrated on near bow-on and stern-on aspects.
verdict.is_0_of_16_faithful: no. It is numerically unsurprising - the shipped bot under-leads twice over, once from the half-b linear coefficient and once from leading at WaterTravelSpeed when the round swims at 0.6 * WaterTravelSpeed - but in this build no torpedo can reach any target at all: src/game_hosts_gunnery.cpp:1582 kills every projectile that crosses y = 0 downward, with no swim phase, which is the 'water' rising by 12 of 16. A correct solver would have changed nothing in this run.

routines.name: BSP_Math_SolveInterceptPoint
routines.abi: __fastcall(ECX const float3* shooter, EDX const float3* target)(float speed, const float3* target_velocity, float3* out) -> bool in AL, RET 0Ch
routines.rule: n = 008FB8D0(shooter, target, speed, target_velocity, &t1, &t2); n==0 -> false with out untouched (008FBC00); n==1 -> t = t1 (008FBB9E); n==2 -> t = t2 (008FBB3C); out = target + t * target_velocity; true
routines.evidence: the listing. The two out pointers at 008FBB0F and 008FBB14 are the caller's own argA and argB stack slots reused as scratch, both read into ST0 and EDI first.

routines.name: BSP_Math_SolveInterceptTime
routines.abi: __fastcall(ECX const float3* shooter, EDX const float3* target)(float speed, const float3* v, float* t_far, float* t_near) -> int in EAX, RET 10h
routines.rule: d = shooter - target (008FB8D3..008FB8EF); a = dot(v,v) - speed*speed (008FB933..008FB945); b = dot(d,v) (008FB949..008FB96B); c = dot(d,d) (008FB96F..008FB97D). |a| <= 1e-4 (00D7A268 / 00D0D098): t = c/b, negative written back as 0.0f, answer 1 (008FB99C..008FB9F7). Otherwise disc = b*b - 4*a*c (008FBA02, the 4 at 00D7A328); disc < 0 -> 0 (008FBA1F); root = sqrt (008FBA21, 00BF7030); a > 0 (008FBA2C against 0.0f at 00D7A218): *t_far = (b+root)/(a+a), else *t_far = (b-root)/(a+a); *t_far < 0 -> 0 after the store (008FBA6D / 008FBABE); the other root into *t_near; answer 2 when *t_near >= 0, else 1 (008FBAE4).
routines.note: b is HALF the exact linear coefficient: the exact intercept is a t^2 - 2*dot(d,v) t + c = 0. docs/GUN_BOT_REMAINDER.md section 2 established this and tests/math_tests.cpp pins it; this packet re-read the listing and agrees. src/gun_bot_remainder.cpp:26-100 reproduces it faithfully.

routines.name: BSP_TurningGun_FilterHeadingToTraverse
routines.abi: __thiscall(gun)(float horz, float limit) -> float in ST0, RET 8
routines.rule: grows the platform array through 005471B0 when [gun+38Ch] is past the count at [[[gun+3F0h]+538h]+94h]+4, then tail-calls 007F6190 on platform [[[gun+3F0h]+538h]+94h][gun+38Ch] with (horz, limit). Argument order confirmed by 0085AB7A/0085AB8A: [ESP+10h] (limit) lands at [ESP+4] and [ESP+14h] (horz) at [ESP].
routines.note: the existing ledger record already had this shape and named 007F6190 contract: unread.

routines.name: BSP_GunPlatform_SnapHeadingToFireWindow
routines.abi: __thiscall(platform)(float horz, float limit) -> float in ST0
routines.rule: scan the arc array at [platform+3Ch], [platform+40h] records of 14h bytes, for the first record whose HORIZONTAL bounds (+4h min, +8h max, widened by 00D08B88 = half a degree) hold horz clamped to +/-pi - no flag test and no vertical test. None -> FLT_MAX (00D08B80). That record carries the fire bit (bit 1) -> horz unchanged. Otherwise walk backwards, then forwards, through records that carry the traverse bit (bit 0); at the first record on each side that also carries the fire bit take its nearer bound by BSP_Math_SubtractWrappedAngle, keep the nearer of the two candidates; no candidate, or |wrapped(candidate - horz)| > limit -> FLT_MAX; else the candidate.
routines.note: the native snaps a heading onto the nearest firing-window edge rather than refusing it. src/gun_aiming.cpp:120 refuses instead, and nothing in the host models the snap.

routines.name: BSP_Torpedo_RecordInitSwimSpeed_fragment
routines.abi: fragment, no Ghidra function; ESI = the torpedo record, [ESI+314h] = the projectile class descriptor
routines.coverage: partial fragment: 0085782E..00857875 inclusive, final instruction FSTP float [ESI+470h]. The enclosing routine has no Ghidra function and was not read.
routines.rule: record+474h = 0.5999994f (00D0C5EC); record+478h = 3.0000007f (00D0C5E8); record+470h = classDesc[+0E4h] * 0.59999943 (00D0C5E0, double) = WaterTravelSpeed * 0.6
routines.evidence: tools/bsp.py scan-bytes 'D9 ?? E4 00 00 00' over .text, filtered to 0084xxxx-0086xxxx, then disasm-raw. 0085786F is mid-instruction; the stream resyncs at 0085786D.

host_calls.what: the torpedo bot's intercept call. ECX = ESP+3Ch (shooter point), EDX = ESP+28h (target point), arg1 = the float from [[gun+3F8h]+34h]+0E4h, arg2 = ESP+48h (the target velocity with y forced to 0.0f at 00900258), arg3 = ESP+64h (the out point). AL checked at 00900263.
the root solve. ECX and EDX pass through unchanged; the two out pointers are the wrapper's own incoming argument slots.
the heading filter, limit = pi/4 from 00E0B588. 0090038D stores the answer at bot+60h; 00900392..009003A2 compares it with FLT_MAX (00D7A278) and abandons the shot at 009003A6 when it matches.
the delegate that does the snap
grows the platform array before the index is used

the torpedo bot commands its angles. arg1 = bot+60h (the filtered heading) from the value left in ST0 across the 009003A2 branch; arg2 = 0.0f, pushed by the FLDZ at 009003CE and stored at 009003D6. THE VERTICAL IS HARD ZERO.

corrections.was: There is no thrust term here and none in 00856BB0, so WaterTravelSpeed (classDesc+E4h) does not reach the swim: the torpedo coasts on the velocity it entered the water with
corrections.is: the clause 'WaterTravelSpeed (classDesc+E4h) does not reach the swim' is REFUTED. 00857834 loads classDesc+0E4h and 00857875 stores WaterTravelSpeed * 0.6 into record+470h, the field that document's own step 6 records the tick tail as reading. The coasting reading came from a listing window that did not contain the initialiser. What record+470h is used for inside the tick is still unread.
corrections.evidence: 0085782E MOV EAX,[ESI+314h]; 00857834 FLD float [EAX+0E4h]; 0085785D FMUL qword [00D0C5E0] = 0.59999943; 00857875 FSTP float [ESI+470h]. The identity descriptor+60h = (record+470h) * FlyTime is exact for the Mark 15: 30.866 * 60 = 1852.0, and 00855A90 uses the same 0.6 at 00CEFF98.

Its value is dominated by mounts parked at their (0,0) rest angles outside a 50-68 degree broadside sector because gun_set_target_angles_0085aba0 refused their target angles on the vertical axis, not by the authored arcs refusing a bearing.
